summary.what_changed: Reworked the `commands` criterion in the CLAUDE.md health auditor (`scripts/claude-md-audit.mjs`). It previously scored 7 points per fenced code block containing a recognized tool keyword, which rewarded fragmenting commands into many small blocks and ignored commands documented in linked `.md` files. The new `countCommandLines()` counts actual executable command lines inside fences (stripping `$ ` prompts, skipping blanks/comments), and `extractDocRefs`/`resolveLinkedCommands` follow backticked-path, markdown-link, and `@import` references to linked docs (bounded to the target root, `.md` only, max 25 files, 256 KB each) and credit their command lines at half weight (capped at 10 of the 20 possible points). The recognized tool-token list was also broadened to cover Python-first tooling (`uv`, `pytest`, `ruff`, `mypy`, `alembic`, `prefect`) alongside existing tokens. `scoreFile()` gains an optional 4th `opts.linkedCommandLines` parameter (default 0); all existing 3-arg call sites are unaffected.
summary.why: A real CLAUDE.md audited at 7/20 on the commands criterion despite thoroughly documenting build/test/run commands, because it consolidated commands into one well-organized fenced block (penalizing consolidation) and referenced 23 linked `.md` docs containing the actual command lines, none of which the auditor read. The criterion was measuring a proxy (fence count) instead of the property it claims to score (does this file tell an agent how to build/test/run), and unrecognized Python tooling made the problem worse for non-JS repos. The fix realigns the metric with intent and was calibrated against the real file (83/B → 96/A, commands 7/20 → 20/20).

doc_targets.notes: Documents the new countCommandLines/extractDocRefs/resolveLinkedCommands scoring mechanism and the `commands = min(20, ownLines*4 + min(10, linkedLines*2))` formula so the audit tool's behavior is discoverable outside the source diff and design spec. No existing architecture/operations section exists under the core lens yet (only images/), so this lands as a flat root page pending a future architecture/ directory.

summary.what_changed: Lands a design spec (CCE-163) proposing a redesign of the Memory & Context Management Execution scorer, plus the telemetry survey and probe-catalog/test updates that back it — no scorer numerator change ships in this PR. The spec documents three measurement defects in the same class as CCE-161's fenced-block-counting bug, surveys 2,019 transcripts over a 30-day window, and finds graphify (127 sessions) as a real but currently uncounted usage signal, while noting claude-mem is passive hook capture (Platform posture, not Execution behavior). It recommends unioning session-coverage across /clear, /compact, graphify invocations, and claude-mem tool_use, gated against interactiveOrUnknownSessionsAnalyzed. One open decision — whether auto-compact configuration should be evidence-only (A) or suppress the manual-command expectation (B) — blocks implementation; the spec recommends (A).
summary.why: Memory & Context Management currently scores Platform 100 / Execution 33, derived from a two-slash-command numerator (70 session-coverage hits / 353 sessions). CCE-79 established design-before-implement as the required pattern before touching a scorer numerator, given the risk of silently corrupting a ratio (as happened with the /btw cumulative-vs-windowed defect). This PR performs that design step for CCE-163: surveying real telemetry to identify undercounted signals before proposing a redesigned numerator, rather than editing score.mjs directly.

summary.what_changed: Fixed the session-kind classifier (`classifySessionKind` in `scripts/_usage-data.mjs`) to fail closed on unrecognized transcript entrypoints. Previously it enumerated known SDK entrypoints and let anything else fall through to `unknown`, which is admitted by the `interactive_or_unknown` posture universe used by Memory & Terminal Execution scoring. An unhandled `sdk-py` entrypoint plus a 5-line scan bound (too shallow for transcripts that lead with `queue-operation`/`attachment` rows) caused 265 of 612 in-window sessions (43%) to misclassify as `unknown`, diluting the Memory Execution denominator to 353 against a true 93 (3.8x) and scoring a well-instrumented machine at 37/100. The fix inverts the classifier to an allow-list (`INTERACTIVE_ENTRYPOINTS = {cli, claude-desktop}`) so every other entrypoint resolves to `observer` or `sdk_orchestrated` instead of `unknown`, and raises the scan bound to `ENTRYPOINT_SCAN_BOUND = 200`.
summary.why: Root cause was a classifier that failed open instead of closed: unknown/unhandled entrypoints and an undersized scan window silently entered a posture-scoring denominator meant to represent only user-driven interactive sessions, producing a severely understated Memory Execution score. Fixing this restores denominator integrity (93 true interactive-or-unknown sessions vs. the inflated 353) and moved Memory Execution 37↚100 and overall Execution 60↚68 on the measured machine.

doc_targets.notes: Postmortem/decision record for CCE-164: documents the fail-open→fail-closed classifier defect, the 3.8x denominator dilution it caused, and the allow-list + scan-bound fix.
